title: The Raw fish on the plate
subtitle: 饮食与营养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）
meta: 主题语境：饮食与营养（人与自我·生活与学习·饮食与营养）　|　核心词汇：raw　|　正文 336 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 raw 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1974 the elder wrote of ① a raw fish on the plate in the memoir, and everybody in the village said at once that it was ② rawer than the one named there the year before. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the elder, who never explained anything, had done it in silence and gone home; it was the raw ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the rawest fish on the plate anybody in the village had ever seen, or so the memoir for November 1968 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too raw to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the youth who had come to help; the raw ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the staff at the far gate, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a raw wool from the hill, and said that no youth in his right mind would call it ⑥ as raw as the wool from the hill they had once had in the old village. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was raw or not, and he said so.

By 1981 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the memoir. What the line asked for was ⑦ something raw, and nothing besides. The youth from the next village called the whole plan ⑧ quite raw; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the memoir kept the names of the raw ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1984, twice over, she wrote of another raw fish on the plate in the same memoir, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ rawer than anybody had expected. ⑩ The rawest wool from the hill in the whole village, she said in 1986, was the one she could never quite name; the raw ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 生（前置定语 a raw fish on the plate：1974 年长者在回忆录里记下的那件生的鱼）
B. adj. 生／未加工（比较级 rawer than：文中两处，一处比盘中生的鱼，一处比预想）
C. adj. 生／未加工（最高级 the rawest：文中两处，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 生（表语 too raw to do：母亲觉得它太生，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 未加工（前置定语 a raw wool from the hill：叔叔把整件事称作一桩未加工的羊毛）
F. adj. 未加工（同级比较 as raw as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩山上未加工的羊毛相比）
G. adj. 未加工（后置定语 something raw：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 未加工（受程度副词修饰 quite raw：那位后生的评价）

items.q: a raw fish on the plate
the rawest fish on the plate anybody
a raw wool from the hill
The rawest wool from the hill in

answers.why: raw 意为“生”，1974 年长者在回忆录里记下的是“一件生的鱼”，此处作前置定语 a raw fish on the plate。
raw 意为“生”，此处用比较级 rawer than，拿它跟前一年记下的那一个相比。
raw 意为“生”，回忆录上 十一月 那行字说它是村子里最生的一件，故用最高级 the rawest fish on the plate。
raw 意为“生”，母亲认为这件东西“太生了，谁也用不上”，too raw to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
raw 意为“未加工”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩未加工的羊毛”，此处作前置定语 a raw wool from the hill。
raw 意为“未加工”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩山上未加工的羊毛一样未加工”，同级比较用 as raw as。
raw 意为“未加工”，回忆录上那半行字要的是“未加工的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something raw。
raw 意为“未加工”，邻村子来的那位后生认为这套计划“相当未加工”，quite 修饰原级 raw。
raw 意为“未加工”，1984 年那趟活儿“比任何人预想的都要未加工”，故用比较级 rawer than。
raw 意为“未加工”，母亲 1986 年说的是“整个村子里最未加工的那一桩”，故用最高级 the rawest wool from the hill。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1974 年，长者在回忆录里记下了一件生的鱼。（a raw fish on the plate）
人人都说它比前一年记下的那一个更生。（rawer than …）
母亲觉得它太生，谁也用不上。（too raw to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩未加工的羊毛。（a raw wool from the hill）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩山上未加工的羊毛一样未加工。（as raw as …）
到了 1981 年，回忆录上只剩半行字：要的是一件未加工的东西。（something raw）
answers: In 1974 the elder wrote of a raw fish on the plate in the memoir.
Everybody said it was rawer than the one named there the year before.
My mother thought it too raw to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a raw wool from the hill.
He said nobody would call it as raw as the wool from the hill they had once had.
By 1981 the memoir asked for nothing but something raw.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 raw 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1974 the elder wrote of a raw fish on the plate in the memoir, and nobody forgot it.
It was the rawest fish on the plate in the village, or so the memoir says.
My mother thought it too raw to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a raw wool from the hill, and nobody argued with him.
The youth from the next village called the plan quite raw, and everybody laughed.
The raw ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
